# CookieGuard security checks

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-schemas.js from the engine catalog. Do not edit. -->

A `confirmed` finding needs a configured authentication cookie and observed attributes; it can fail a run.
A `review` finding is heuristic or uncertain and never fails a run.

## CG001 Missing HttpOnly (high)

- Checks: HttpOnly
- Confirmed when: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed without HttpOnly.
- Review when: A cookie that only heuristics suggest is authentication-related lacks HttpOnly.
- Why: If accepted, a cookie without HttpOnly can be read by JavaScript. This increases token exposure if script execution is compromised; it does not demonstrate XSS.
- Fix: Set HttpOnly on the authentication cookie at the server.

## CG002 Missing Secure (high)

- Checks: Secure
- Confirmed when: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed without Secure.
- Review when: A cookie that only heuristics suggest is authentication-related lacks Secure.
- Why: The cookie is not restricted to HTTPS transport. This is a configuration exposure, not proof of interception.
- Fix: Set Secure and serve the application over HTTPS.

## CG003 SameSite declaration violates policy (medium)

- Checks: SameSite
- Confirmed when: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed with a declared SameSite value outside allowedSameSite, or with no declaration while requireExplicitSameSite is set.
- Review when: The same condition on a cookie whose authentication role is unconfirmed.
- Why: The declared cross-site behavior does not meet the configured policy. SameSite alone does not establish CSRF protection or vulnerability.
- Fix: Use an allowed SameSite value, or explicitly adjust the policy for a reviewed cross-site flow with separate CSRF defenses.

## CG004 Domain sharing requires review (medium)

- Checks: Domain scope
- Confirmed when: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed with a Domain attribute while requireHostOnly is set.
- Review when: A Domain attribute without requireHostOnly, or on a cookie whose role is unconfirmed.
- Why: A Domain attribute shares the cookie with matching subdomains. This does not establish subdomain compromise or takeover.
- Fix: Omit Domain when subdomain sharing is unnecessary; use a valid __Host- cookie where practical.

## CG005 Authentication-cookie lifetime exceeds policy (medium)

- Checks: Client lifetime
- Confirmed when: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed with a remaining lifetime above maxLifetimeDays.
- Review when: The same condition on a cookie whose authentication role is unconfirmed.
- Why: A longer client lifetime extends potential exposure. Server-side session expiry and revocation are not measured.
- Fix: Reduce Max-Age or Expires to the configured maximum and enforce server-side session expiry.

## CG006 Invalid security prefix declaration (high)

- Checks: __Host- and __Secure- prefixes
- Confirmed when: The cookie is a confirmed authentication cookie (an exact configured authCookies name or validated authEvidence) and the attribute was observed in a Set-Cookie header that violates its prefix requirements.
- Review when: The same header violation on a cookie whose authentication role is unconfirmed.
- Why: The observed header violates __Host- or __Secure- requirements. Browsers may reject it; this does not prove an insecure cookie was accepted.
- Fix: Use HTTPS and Secure for both prefixes; __Host- also requires an explicit Path=/ and no Domain.

## CG007 Authentication-cookie protection regressed (high)

- Checks: Baseline regression
- Confirmed when: A comparable baseline shows that a confirmed authentication cookie lost Secure, HttpOnly, host-only scope, a Lax/Strict SameSite declaration, or its lifetime limit.
- Review when: Never; incomparable baselines produce no CG007 findings.
- Why: Comparable observations show a previously enabled protection was removed.
- Fix: Restore the previous protection or review and document the intentional policy change.

## CG008 Authentication role is unconfirmed (info)

- Checks: Authentication identity
- Confirmed when: Never; this is always a review item.
- Review when: A cookie looks like authentication to the uncalibrated classifier, or its role is unknown, and it was not configured.
- Why: Classifier outputs are triage signals, not validated probabilities of an authentication role.
- Fix: Identify the actual session cookie in your login test and configure its exact name or validated scoped evidence.

## CG009 Cookie evidence requires review (info)

- Checks: Evidence quality
- Confirmed when: Never; this is always a review item.
- Review when: Attributes, the SameSite declaration, or browser acceptance are unknown or ambiguous.
- Why: Some attributes, declarations, or browser acceptance are unknown or ambiguous.
- Fix: Start collection before login and inspect the server cookie configuration. Do not infer declarations from browser defaults.

## Incomplete reasons

- `collection-incomplete`: The collector stopped early, hit a limit, or produced provisional evidence. Start collection before the login, let the workflow finish, then evaluate once. Provisional agent checks never satisfy policy.
- `no-cookies-observed`: The audited response or workflow set no cookies. Audit the endpoint or login workflow that creates the session, and start collection before it runs.
- `expected-auth-cookie-not-observed`: At least one configured authCookies name was not set during the audit. Check the exact cookie name and audit the response or workflow that issues the session cookie.
- `validated-auth-cookie-not-observed`: A cookie listed in authEvidence was not observed with the same name, domain, path, and origin. Update authEvidence or audit the workflow that issues that scoped cookie.
- `scan-not-completed`: An error stopped the audit before a decision; see error.code. Explain the error code, correct the cause, and rerun. Do not treat the run as passed.

Secure example: `Set-Cookie: session_id=<opaque>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`
